words.sense: A vague, difficult-to-explain feeling of unease, weariness, or dissatisfaction.
misconceptions: Treating comfort or a full schedule as proof against weariness.
Missing when monotony specifically explains dissatisfaction.

words.sense: Weariness and dissatisfaction arising specifically from boredom.
misconceptions: Calling any low mood boredom even without a cause.
Missing when monotony specifically explains dissatisfaction.

semantic_axes.description: Malaise is a diffuse unease without a clear cause, whereas ennui is dissatisfaction caused by boredom or lack of stimulation.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Nikhil’s mood on Saturday morning?

beats.text: Nikhil woke drained and unsettled, although he had slept well and looked forward to the day’s plans.
beats.reason: Unexplained unease despite anticipated activities. A vague, difficult-to-explain feeling of unease, weariness, or dissatisfaction.

beats.text: The unsettled feeling followed him through breakfast, even though he left home on time.
beats.decisive_clue: punctuality does not explain or remove the same unsettled feeling
beats.reason: Punctuality does not explain or remove the same unsettled feeling. A vague, difficult-to-explain feeling of unease, weariness, or dissatisfaction.

chains.feedback_short: Punctuality does not explain or remove the same unsettled feeling.
chains.feedback_deep: Malaise means a vague, difficult-to-explain feeling of unease, weariness, or dissatisfaction; ennui means weariness and dissatisfaction arising specifically from boredom. Here, unexplained unease despite anticipated activities. The new detail does not change the deciding fact: punctuality does not explain or remove the same unsettled feeling. Thus malaise remains the stronger choice.
chains.contrast_rule: Malaise has no clear source; ennui grows from having too little to engage you.
